references.text: God promises to meet Israel at the entrance of the tent of meeting, where he will speak with them and reveal his glory.
The incense altar is to be placed in front of the curtain that is by the ark of the testimony, before the mercy seat where God will meet with Moses.
The description of the mercy seat and the cherubim to be made of gold and placed on the ark of the testimony.
God reveals himself in the cloud above the mercy seat and warns Aaron not to enter the Most Holy Place at any time.
Moses heard God's voice speaking to him from the mercy seat between the two cherubim, fulfilling the promise in Exodus 25:22.
The ark of the covenant is referred to as the place where the Lord reigns between the cherubim.
David and the people bring up the ark, which is called by the name of the Lord, he who reigns above the cherubim.
Hezekiah prays to the Lord who reigns above the cherubim and acknowledges him as the only God.
A prayer to the Shepherd of Israel who reigns above the cherubim, asking him to reveal his glory.
The Lord is king and reigns above the cherubim, demonstrating his majesty and holiness.
Hezekiah prays to the Lord, the God of hosts, who reigns above the cherubim.
The author mentions the glorious cherubim that overshadow the mercy seat in the earthly tabernacle.
Both confirm that the tent of meeting before the testimony is the fixed place where God reveals himself to his people.
Theological complementarity: The atonement cover is the meeting place (Exodus), and atonement is the prerequisite for standing there (Leviticus).
Direct textual repetition confirming the consecration of the meeting place for all Israel.
